title: Join waitlist button: follows your scroll at the top too; the end of the page stays as in rev 1
problem:
Rev 2, answering your notes on rev 1:
- "SOOOO ULTRA SMOOTH on the end of page": kept. The end-of-page part is the same two rules as rev 1, unchanged.
- "the button will appear when we scroll down. it still lag a bit": yes. At the top, the button runs on its own clock.
- It starts only when the hero is 72 % scrolled, then reaches full width about 0.6 s later.
- Its text then sweeps in until about 1.5 s, even if you stopped scrolling.
- "you didn't apply this on the scroll on the top of page": correct, rev 1 only changed the end of the page.
- "open new thread": the full trace is in the catch-up thread (T-154).
idea:
The button now follows your finger at the top too, like at the end of the page:
1. While the hero goes from 58 % to 72 % scrolled, the button grows from nothing to full: width, fade and the left-to-right text sweep all follow the scroll position.
2. At 72 %, where the bar used to start its own 0.6 s animation, the button is already full, so nothing jumps or keeps moving.
3. Scrolling back up shrinks it the same way, with the scroll.
The end-of-page part is rev 1, unchanged. The shine that passes over the button keeps its own timing.
looksSame:
At rest it is the same picture as today's best build (v8).
- Same: the hero at the top, the full bar further down, the end panel.
- Different on purpose: the button grows during the scroll just before the bar changes, instead of after it.
visualDiff:
Top of the page: the button appears over the last stretch of the hero scroll (58-72 %), following the finger.
- Before: nothing until 72 %, then a 0.6 s grow and a sweep until 1.5 s.
A very fast flick that jumps over the whole stretch in one frame shows the old 0.6 s grow (the text shows at once).
End of page: unchanged from rev 1 (the part you liked).

risk:
Low: one small style block and 7 lines of script on top of rev 1.
- The script writes one number on two elements while the hero is 58-72 % scrolled, and only when it changes; outside that stretch it writes nothing.
- The button now starts to show a bit earlier (at 58 % instead of 72 %); that is what makes it follow the finger.
- Reduced motion: unchanged (the bar never uses the hero state there).
- Safari check of rev 2 in the iOS Simulator: still running, result by about 21:10Z in this proposal's comments.
